title: Question about refit
body:
Hi,
I am now applying the refit method on my pre-trained model(model A) with new data (model B after). However, it performs worse than model A on a valid dataset. I know it could happen, but is it possible to tune the parameters during refitting to get a better result? Or my question also can be explained as Should I use the very same parameters during refitting?
author: PsLiKrypt

comments.body:
could you provide the code about how you do it?
It model B is tested over "new data", you should be better than model A.
But for valid data, it is hard to say. if it is closer to data of the pretrain, the refit could not improve it.

Thanks for replying!
Well, I use the CLI version of lightgbm so it's hard to provide the code. In more details, I train model A over 7 days data, say, Sep.15 to Sep.21, model A, which will be used during Sep.22 all day.
Every hours I can collect realtime brand new data. Now I want to  update it within Sep.22. Since 'refit' is quit faster than just retraining a new model over 7 plus half days data, if I do this in the middle of Sep.22, I try using the data from half of Sep.22 to refit the model A to get model B. Another half data is my valid data, and I calculate AUC(in turn AUC_A, AUC_B).  Parameters in configure files are the same except 'task'.
The result is, AUC_B is smaller than AUC_A.  
Do you have any advice to help me flip this result? :)

I feel like the distribution of two halves (let us donate them to p and q) in one day is much different.
So it is possible the model B is fit to p. So I think a more reasonable usage is to update it per day, not per half day.

> I feel like the distribution of two halves (let us donate them to p and q) in one day is much different.
> So it is possible the model B is fit to p. So I think a more reasonable usage is to update it per day, not per half day.

I guess you are right. 
Now I only have a small question. Can I change some parameters when refitting? Or I should keep them to be the same.
I think the only parameter in refit is refit_decay. Others are not used.

satisfaction_conditions: Clarification on which parameters can be modified during model refitting
Explanation for why the refitted model might perform worse on validation data
Practical advice on appropriate time intervals for model updates

title: a question about lightgbm for lambdarank
author: RobotZZZZZ

comments.body: @RobotZZZZZ this normalization is for different queries, to avoid the result dominated by query with large scores.

hi@guolinke ,
so far as I know, ndcg is normalized dcg in range [0, 1]. why we need normalize again?

@guolinke I think about it. 
You means, when training model, we don't want that training is dominated by query with large scores, maybe model is hard to rank them right. we want model focus on what it can do.

@RobotZZZZZ 
yeah, it is similar the `log` or `sqrt` trick for regression program, avoid the bad effect of outliers.

satisfaction_conditions: Explanation of the purpose behind LightGBM's normalization of NDCG by score distance in lambdarank
Technical justification for the additional normalization beyond NDCG's inherent [0,1] range
Explanation of the practical benefits this normalization provides in model training
